A tree-diagram classifying the 16 essential plant nutrients. The top box says "Essential Plant Nutrients". It splits into two branches: "Macronutrients (Needed in large amounts)" and "Micronutrients (Needed in trace amounts)". The Macronutrients box splits into "Air and Water: C, H, O", "Primary: N, P, K", and "Secondary: Ca, Mg, S". The Micronutrients box lists "Fe, Zn, Cu, Mn, B, Mo, Cl".

A side-by-side illustration of fertilizer application methods. Left: a hand scattering granular fertilizer randomly over a grassy field ("Broadcasting"). Middle: a maize plant with a straight line of fertilizer placed next to its base ("Row Placement"). Right: a small cocoa tree with a circular trench dug around it containing fertilizer ("Ring Application").
